column4: Visit note | 2026-03-28 10:00 AM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Tuhin Kabir, 73, male. Mr. Kabir attends for review of his ongoing breathing issues, mentioning increased wheezing when walking and breathlessness that has been worse for several days. He is a homemaker and explains his symptoms worsened after a cold caught at a crowded market in Cox's Bazar. He has a long history of smoking and denies chest pain or lower limb swelling. On examination: SpO2 87%, BP 134/86 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 49 kg. Chest auscultation reveals widespread expiratory wheeze with reduced air entry at the bases. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued for his care. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.
